newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NANTES CHARTER PLANE TO COLLECT YOUNG GOALKEEPER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NANTES CHARTER PLANE TO COLLECT YOUNG GOALKEEPER.

text.p: Nantes may have finally found their goal touch but regard teenage goalkeeper Mickael Landreau as equally important in their incipient revival.

The 1995 French champions, who ended a 10-match run without a win by trouncing Nice 7-0 last weekend, are flying Landreau in from international duty with the national under-18 side in Sweden for the match at Lille on Saturday.

A private jet chartered by Nantes was due to pick up Landreau on Friday evening. The youngster has not been beaten in his first two first division outings since injury deprived Nantes of Dominique Casagrande.
Landreau has greatly steadied the Nantes defence with assured performances that included a penalty save in his debut in a 0-0 draw at Bastia 11 days ago.
"Not a goal conceded in two matches. Things look clear to me, we are much better at the back," coach Jean Claude Suaudeau said.
"And we're getting the ball forward quickly where we are no longer hesitant in our movements.
"However, our convalescence is not over and we have to consolidate all this. A point at Lille would be a logical step and with three points I might start to think of Spring."
The forwards, seven of whom made the scoresheet against Nice, are also being cautious.
Jocelyn Gourvennec, who opened the floodgates, said: "Our victory against Nice means nothing if we don't become consistent. To have scored seven or 10 last Saturday doesn't change the standings."

Nantes, 17th and still in the relegation zone after losing France internationals Reynald Pedros and Nicolas Ouedec to Marseille and Espanyol of Barcelona respectively, have yet to win away. Twelfth-placed Lille are unbeaten at home.

"Things are still worrying and we have to string together some good performances to get out of the hole. We'll have to keep that in mind at Lille or we risk coming down with a bump," midfielder Gourvennec added.

Defender Christophe Pignol said: "We had to get our feet back on the ground. Every game is going to be a battle, but the victory against Nice lightened the atmosphere in and around the club and the pressure has seemed easier to bear."
Nantes are still without injured Argentine striker Javier Mazzoni and central defender Laurent Guyot, but Tunisian international Adel Sellimi is back from African Nations' Cup duty.

Lille, who last won the championship in 1954, hope to have their French under-21 forward Djezon Boutoille back from injury. Zaire's Roger Hitoto is injured and fellow midfielder Thierry Rabat suspended.
